Split the outer conjunction and each biconditional. In both biconditionals, prove the two sides independently, since all four universal statements are standard facts.

- For the alternating group, use `Nat.card α ≥ 3` to choose three distinct elements. Their 3-cycle is even and nonidentity, giving two distinct elements of the alternating group subtype.
- For \(p>0\), apply the standard characterization
  \[
  \varphi(p)=p-1 \iff p\text{ is prime}.
  \]
- For a nonzero prime ideal \(P\) in a Dedekind domain, rewrite quotient cardinality as the ideal norm and use multiplicativity:
  \[
  |S/P^i|=N(P^i)=N(P)^i=|S/P|^i.
  \]
  The nonzero assumption is essential for the finite quotient/norm statement.
- For \(n:\mathrm{PNat}\), use that \(1\) is the gcd identity, so \(\gcd(n,1)=1\).

Thus each `Iff` follows by pairing proofs of its two already-valid sides; no mathematical conversion between the unrelated sides is needed.
